topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic serves as the lecture opening, introducing the lecturer, the course structure, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Intrinsic, Genetic, and Evolutionary Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the core concept of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by endogenous mutational processes, replication errors, and inherited genetic predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental Factors, Epidemiology, and the Cancer Risk Debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore external environmental exposures, the debate over biological chance versus external carcinogens, and population-level epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Biological and Chemical Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the direct and indirect mechanisms through which infectious pathogens, dietary toxins, xenobiotic metabolism, chronic inflammation, tumor promoters, and developmental susceptibility drive cancer formation.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo animal, and in vitro experimental methods used to identify, measure, and prove the carcinogenicity of specific agents.

topics.label: Lecture Wrap-Up and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing for the lecture, summarizing the central themes of environmental exposure and balancing everyday risks against benefits.
